title: The Art of Staying Ahead of Deadlines Improved Algorithms for the Minimum Tardy Processing Time

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Lemma 3.2 states "∑_{i∈[n]} |S̃_j \ S_{j-1}| ≤ d_max+1" — the summation index is written as i, but the summand depends on j, which is never bound by the sum. The same mismatch recurs throughout the proof (e.g., "|{i ∈ [n] | x ∈ S̃_j \ S_{j-1}}| ≤ 1" and "∑_{i∈[n]} |S̃_j \ S_{j-1}| = ∑_{x∈[0..d_max]} |{i ∈ [n] | x ∈ S̃_j \ S_{j-1}}|"). This makes the statement as written mathematically ill-formed; it should consistently use j as the summation variable, as is correctly done in the analogous Lemma 4.1 ("∑_{j∈[n]} |S̃_j \ S_{j-1}| ≤ (d_max+1)^m").

The text defines the reduced problem as finding J* ⊆ [n] maximizing ∑_{j∈J*} p_j subject to "∑_{i∈J*:i≤j} p_i ≤ d_j for all j ∈ J", but the symbol J is never defined anywhere in the paper (only J* and [n] are introduced). If J is meant to be the full index set [n], the deadline constraint would be required to hold even for indices not in J*, which contradicts the stated intent of only "observ[ing] the deadlines of the jobs within J*"; if J is meant to be J*, the notation is simply wrong/undefined.
